proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\) and put \(\delta=1/2-\eta\).  We first construct one interior point of the asserted family.  Let
\[
 b(z)=c_b\exp\{-1/(1-z^2)\}\mathbf 1\{|z|<1\},
 \qquad m_2=\int_{-1}^1z^2b(z)\,dz,
\]
where \(c_b\) normalizes the density.  Symmetry gives \(\mathbb E Z=0\), and strict positivity on \((-1,1)\) gives \(0<m_2<1\).  Let
\[
 \beta(t)=c_\beta\exp\{-1/[t(1-t)]\}\mathbf 1\{0<t<1\},
 \qquad L=3,
\]
with \(c_\beta\) again chosen to give integral one.  Define the strictly positive numbers
\[
 e_\eta=\frac{\delta m_2}{64L^2},\qquad
 v_\eta=L^2e_\eta(1-e_\eta),\qquad
 B_\eta=\frac{\delta v_\eta}{256},
\]
and then
\[
 h_\eta=\sqrt{B_\eta/8},
 \qquad \tau_\eta=\frac{B_\eta}{2L^2}.
\]
Because \(0<\delta<1/2\), \(0<m_2<1\), and \(L=3\), these choices satisfy \(0<e_\eta<1/2\), \(0<h_\eta<1/4\), and \(0<\tau_\eta<1\).  On \([0,L]\), set
\[
 p_\eta(x)=(1-\tau_\eta)
 \left\{(1-e_\eta)h_\eta^{-1}\beta(x/h_\eta)
 +e_\eta h_\eta^{-1}\beta((L-x)/h_\eta)\right\}
 +\frac{\tau_\eta}{L}. \tag{15}
\]
The bump terms in (15) are zero off their indicated endpoint bands.  Let \(X\) have density \(p_\eta\), let \(N\) have density \(b\), take \(X\perp N\), and set
\[
 Y=X+N. \tag{16}
\]
The node domains are \([0,L]\) and \([-1,L+1]\), and the generating graph is \(X\to Y\).

We verify membership in \(\mathcal M_0(2)\), including its identification restriction.  The functions \(b\), \(\beta\), and \(p_\eta\) are \(C^\infty\) on their relative interiors; \(b\) is positive on \((-1,1)\), and the bridge term makes \(p_\eta\) positive on all of \((0,L)\).  Equation (16) has a nonconstant \(C^\infty\) mechanism, independent innovations, and
\[
 [0,L]+[-1,1]=[-1,L+1],
\]
so Assumptions \(\ref{ass:anm-independence}\), \(\ref{ass:smooth-mechanisms}\), \(\ref{ass:smooth-positive-densities}\), \(\ref{ass:support-closure}\), and \(\ref{ass:causal-minimality}\) hold.  The root support and every bivariate conditional-support fiber have connected relative interior.  Both variances are positive, so Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\) holds for this model with any positive lower bound smaller than their minimum.

It remains to check the Condition 19 configuration.  Write \(\xi=\log p_\eta\), \(\nu=\log b\), and
\[
 \Lambda(x,y)=\xi(x)+\nu(y-x)
\]
on the interior of the joint support.  If a reverse additive-noise representation existed locally, then for some functions \(g\), \(r\), and \(s\) its log-density would have the form
\[
 \Lambda(x,y)=r(x-g(y))+s(y).
\]
At points where \(\Lambda_{xx}\ne0\), direct differentiation would give
\[
 \frac{\Lambda_{xy}}{\Lambda_{xx}}=-g'(y),
 \qquad
 \partial_x\left(\frac{\Lambda_{xy}}{\Lambda_{xx}}\right)=0. \tag{17}
\]
Thus failure of (17) is precisely the required local differential obstruction.  For the forward density,
\[
 \Lambda_{xx}=\xi''(x)+\nu''(y-x),
 \qquad \Lambda_{xy}=-\nu''(y-x).
\]
Since \(b\) is symmetric, \(\nu'''(0)=0\), while direct differentiation of \(\nu(z)=\log c_b-1/(1-z^2)\) gives \(\nu''(0)=-2\ne0\).  Hence at \(y=x\), whenever the denominator is nonzero,
\[
 \partial_x\left(\frac{\Lambda_{xy}}{\Lambda_{xx}}\right)
 =\frac{\nu''(0)\xi'''(x)}{\{\xi''(x)+\nu''(0)\}^2}. \tag{18}
\]
There exists \(x\in(0,h_\eta)\) for which the right side of (18) is nonzero.  Indeed, if \(\xi'''\) vanished throughout \((0,h_\eta)\), then \(\xi\) would be quadratic there.  Flatness of the bump at \(h_\eta\) gives \(\xi'(h_\eta-)=\xi''(h_\eta-)=0\), forcing that quadratic to be constant, contrary to the nonconstant bump in (15).  Thus the open set \(\{x:\xi'''(x)\ne0\}\) is nonempty.  The identity \(\xi''(x)+\nu''(0)=0\) cannot hold throughout any component of that open set, because differentiating it would give \(\xi'''=0\).  This proves the assertion.  Continuity makes (18) nonzero on an interior open patch.  Assumption \(\ref{ass:condition19-configurations}\) therefore holds, as does Assumption \(\ref{ass:connected-support-fibers}\).  The constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M_0(2)\), and Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) identifies its labelled graph as \(X\to Y\).

We next bound the two correlation ratios.  Couple \(X\) to \(X_0\in\{0,L\}\) as follows.  On the two bump components use their corresponding endpoint; on the bridge component draw \(X_0=L\) with probability \(e_\eta\), independently of the bridge draw, and otherwise take \(X_0=0\).  Then \(\mathbb P(X_0=L)=e_\eta\), \(\operatorname{Var}(X_0)=v_\eta\), and
\[
 \mathbb E(X-X_0)^2
 \le h_\eta^2+L^2\tau_\eta
 =\frac{5B_\eta}{8}<B_\eta. \tag{19}
\]
The reverse triangle inequality in \(L^2\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, yields
\[
 \left|\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(X)}-\sqrt{v_\eta}\right|
 \le \left\|(X-\mathbb EX)-(X_0-\mathbb EX_0)\right\|_2
 \le2\|X-X_0\|_2<2\sqrt{B_\eta}. \tag{20}
\]
Since \(B_\eta/v_\eta=\delta/256<1/512\), (20) implies the convenient bounds
\[
 \frac12v_\eta<\operatorname{Var}(X)<2v_\eta. \tag{21}
\]
Independence and \(\mathbb EN=0\) give \(\mathbb E[Y\mid X]=X\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(Y)=\operatorname{Var}(X)+m_2\).  Definitions \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) and \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\), followed by (21), therefore give
\[
 q(Y,\{X\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{\operatorname{Var}(X)+m_2}
 \le\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{m_2}
 <\frac{2v_\eta}{m_2}
 \le\frac{2L^2e_\eta}{m_2}
 =\frac{\delta}{32}. \tag{22}
\]

For the reverse prediction problem, use
\[
 \widehat X(Y)=0\quad\text{if }Y<L/2,
 \qquad
 \widehat X(Y)=L\quad\text{if }Y\ge L/2.
\]
Because \(h_\eta<1/4\) and the noise support is \([-1,1]\), this rule classifies both bump components correctly.  Its squared error is at most \(h_\eta^2\) on them and at most \(L^2\) on the bridge.  Conditional-mean optimality in Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\), (19), and (21) imply
\[
 R_{X,\{Y\}}=\mathbb E\operatorname{Var}(X\mid Y)
 \le h_\eta^2+L^2\tau_\eta<B_\eta,
\]
and consequently
\[
 1-q(X,\{Y\})
 =\frac{R_{X,\{Y\}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 <\frac{2B_\eta}{v_\eta}
 =\frac{\delta}{128}. \tag{23}
\]
Combining (22) and (23),
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})
 >\frac12-\frac{\delta}{256}-\frac{\delta}{32}
 =\frac12-\frac{9\delta}{256}
 >\frac12-\delta=\eta. \tag{24}
\]

We now thicken the construction by primitive strict inequalities.  This also makes the meaning of relative openness explicit.  On each fixed graph stratum, transport every compact interval affinely to a reference interval and use the product of: Euclidean convergence of support endpoints, uniform \(C^1\) and compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of mechanisms, and \(L^1\) plus compact-open \(C^3\) convergence of innovation densities.  Give the finitely many graph strata the discrete topology.  This is the structural topology used below.

For a two-node model in the \(X\to Y\) stratum, write the root and child-noise support intervals as \([a,b]\) and \([c,d]\), write the mechanism as \(g\), and put \(r_\eta=2h_\eta\).  Define the endpoint bands
\[
 A_0=[a,a+r_\eta],\qquad A_1=[b-r_\eta,b],
\]
whenever \(b-a>2r_\eta\), and define
\[
 B_{\mathrm{cl}}=r_\eta^2+(b-a)^2
 \mathbb P\{X\notin A_0\cup A_1\}. \tag{25}
\]
Let \(\mathcal U_\eta\) consist of the members of \(\mathcal M_0(2)\) in this stratum for which
\[
 \inf_{x\in[a,b]}g'(x)>0, \tag{26}
\]
\[
 \sup_{x\in A_0}g(x)+d
 <\inf_{x\in A_1}g(x)+c, \tag{27}
\]
\[
 \frac{B_{\mathrm{cl}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}<\frac{\delta}{16}, \tag{28}
\]
and
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}+\operatorname{Var}(N)}
 <\frac{\delta}{16}. \tag{29}
\]
These conditions expose the variables and all divisions: the denominators in (28) and (29) are positive by Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\), and child-noise variance is positive because its density is positive on a nondegenerate interval.

The set \(\mathcal U_\eta\) is relatively open.  Conditions (26)--(29) are strict; extrema in (26)--(27), probabilities and variances in (25), (28), and (29), and their positive-denominator ratios are continuous in the stated topology.  At the reference model (15)--(16), the mass outside \([0,2h_\eta]\cup[L-2h_\eta,L]\) is at most \(\tau_\eta\), so
\[
 B_{\mathrm{cl}}\le4h_\eta^2+L^2\tau_\eta=B_\eta.
\]
Equations (21)--(22) imply (28)--(29).  Moreover, (26) holds with derivative one, and (27) follows from
\[
 2h_\eta+1<L-2h_\eta-1,
\]
which is equivalent to \(h_\eta<1/4\).  Thus the reference law lies in \(\mathcal U_\eta\), proving that this relatively open set is nonempty.

Every law in \(\mathcal U_\eta\) obeys the desired strict margin by the same two elementary risk bounds, without appealing to continuity of the score.  Choose a threshold strictly between the two sides of (27), predict \(a\) below it and \(b\) above it.  On \(A_0\cup A_1\) the squared error is at most \(r_\eta^2\), and outside it the squared error is at most \((b-a)^2\).  Hence (25), conditional-mean optimality, and (28) give
\[
 1-q(X,\{Y\})
 =\frac{R_{X,\{Y\}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 \le\frac{B_{\mathrm{cl}}}{\operatorname{Var}(X)}
 <\frac{\delta}{16}. \tag{30}
\]
By independent additive noise,
\[
 q(Y,\{X\})
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}}
 {\operatorname{Var}\{g(X)\}+\operatorname{Var}(N)}
 <\frac{\delta}{16}. \tag{31}
\]
Equations (30)--(31) yield
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})
 >\frac12-\frac{\delta}{32}-\frac{\delta}{16}
 =\frac12-\frac{3\delta}{32}>\eta. \tag{32}
\]

Reverse residual dependence holds at every point of \(\mathcal U_\eta\) by support geometry, not by continuity of an independence indicator.  Positivity of the two densities on their interval interiors and strict increase in (26) imply that, for
\[
 y\in\bigl(g(a)+c,\,\min\{g(a)+d,g(b)+c\}\bigr),
\]
an interval of positive \(P_Y\)-measure, the relative interior of the conditional support is
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(X\mid Y=y)^\circ
 =\bigl(a,g^{-1}(y-c)\bigr). \tag{33}
\]
Its diameter \(g^{-1}(y-c)-a\) is strictly increasing in \(y\).  Subtracting \(\mathbb E[X\mid Y=y]\) translates (33) and does not alter its diameter.  If \(X-\mathbb E[X\mid Y]\) were independent of \(Y\), its regular conditional distribution, hence its closed support and support diameter, would be the same for \(P_Y\)-almost every \(y\), contradicting (33).  Assumption \(\ref{ass:characteristic-kernels}\) and Definition \(\ref{def:hsic}\) therefore give
\[
 H(X,\{Y\},Y)>0 \tag{34}
\]
throughout \(\mathcal U_\eta\).  No continuity at the independence boundary is asserted or needed.

The family genuinely lies in the broad nonlinear-ANM regime.  For example, replace the identity mechanism at the reference point by
\[
 g_s(x)=x+s x(L-x).
\]
For every sufficiently small nonzero \(s\), this mechanism is non-affine and \(C^3\), maps \([0,L]\) monotonically onto itself, preserves (26)--(29), and preserves the strict differential failure (18) by compact-open \(C^3\) continuity.  Hence these perturbations remain in \(\mathcal U_\eta\cap\mathcal M_0(2)\).

It remains to translate the inequalities into the GENE landscape.  In the causal order \((X,Y)\), the residual of \(Y\) on \(X\) is \(N-\mathbb EN\), independent of \(X\), so Definitions \(\ref{def:hsic}\)--\(\ref{def:gene-score}\) give
\[
 S_P(X,Y)=q(Y,\{X\}). \tag{35}
\]
In the reverse order, (34) makes the dependence count equal to one, and therefore
\[
 S_P(Y,X)=\frac12q(X,\{Y\}). \tag{36}
\]
By (32), (36) is strictly larger than (35).  There are only two labelled orders, so \((Y,X)\) is the unique global maximizer and hence the unique insertion-local maximizer, even though Lemma \(\ref{lem:compact-identifiability}\) identifies \(X\to Y\) for every member of \(\mathcal U_\eta\).

Finally, Definition \(\ref{def:correlation-ratio}\) gives \(0\le q\le1\).  Consequently every nondegenerate bivariate law satisfies
\[
 \frac12q(X,\{Y\})-q(Y,\{X\})\le\frac12. \tag{37}
\]
For every \(\eta<1/2\), (32) supplies a member with difference larger than \(\eta\).  Thus the supremum over \(\bigcup_{0<\eta<1/2}\mathcal U_\eta\) equals \(1/2\), proving sharpness.

proposed.comparator_claim: Li et al. implement Equation (6) with learned neural-network regressions and residual-independence test p-values, and Theorem 4.3 assumes a global strict fitness ranking whenever two orders have different ancestral-reversal counts before concluding recovery under that premise.
The terminal-node normalized explained variance in a random linear causal chain converges to one under a positive mean log-edge-weight condition.
A causally minimal restricted additive-noise model satisfying the Condition 19 configuration requirement has a DAG identifiable from its observational distribution.
Greedy sparsest-permutation algorithms are pointwise consistent under faithfulness through weakly decreasing covered-arrow walks.
Sample splitting gives a fitted-residual dHSIC statistic the same asymptotic null distribution as its exact-residual counterpart.
Studentized cross-HSIC converges to a standard normal law under fixed bounded-kernel null distributions satisfying a second-moment condition.
A likelihood order estimator is consistent when the minimum wrong-order log-residual-variance gap is positive.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparison must distinguish Li et al.'s released finite-sample neural-network and p-value score from the exact population-oracle analogue analyzed here, and must state the matching-subclass success and broad-class existential witnesses without claiming a universal result or a refutation of their conditional theorem.

prose_updates.tldr: For the exact \(\alpha=1\) population-oracle analogue of GENE Equation (6), a primitive edgewise inequality on support-closed matching-component additive-noise models forces a positive reversal-correcting insertion at every wrong order, so best improvement and independence pruning recover the labelled DAG with a finite oracle-query budget. This is a certified success region, not a theorem for Li et al.'s full nonlinear class. Sharpness is witnessed by an explicitly parameterized relatively open bivariate family: for every \(\eta<1/2\), the identifiable causal model \(X\to Y\) has the wrong order as its unique global maximizer with score advantage at least \(\eta\), and \(1/2\) is the universal upper boundary. Cross-fitted simultaneous bands abstain at unresolved independence labels; on separated labels, \(w_S\le K_d w_R\) with \(K_d=O(d/\underline v)\), and the sufficient sample size is \(n\gtrsim\log(M_d/\alpha)\max\{(d/\delta_{\mathrm{pair}})^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},\lambda^{-(d+5)/3}\}\), with the score-margin elbow at \(d=7\) and no minimax claim.

project_justification.gap: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6)) use finite-sample neural-network fits and residual-independence p-values, while their Theorem 4.3 assumes a global score ranking across orders with different ancestral-reversal counts. Peters et al. (2014) identify restricted additive-noise models through Condition 19 configurations, but observational identifiability alone supplies neither local ascent nor protection against a wrong population-score optimum. Existing work also does not provide simultaneous learned-risk and residual-HSIC uncertainty propagation for adaptive GENE search.
project_justification.niche: The useful boundary has three auditable pieces: a structural success certificate with finite population-query complexity, a genuinely open set of identifiable mechanisms on which the exact population score fails as sharply as its range permits, and finite-sample confidence logic that returns a singleton only when navigation and pruning margins are resolved.
project_justification.fill: On the matching-component subclass, the forward-versus-reverse edge signal inequality gives a strict correcting-gain bound and labelled-DAG oracle recovery. A six-node nonlinear witness separates this certificate from Li et al.'s global ranking premise, while a rare-component bivariate construction and its non-affine perturbations produce, for every \(\eta<1/2\), an open trapped-order family with advantage at least \(\eta\). Simultaneous bands yield \(w_S\le K_d w_R\), explicit margin conditions, the \(d=7\) score-rate elbow, and set-valued abstention near independence.

prose_updates.related_work: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6), Definition 4.1, and Theorem 4.3 with its proof on page 5) define the released finite-sample score using neural-network prediction and residual-independence test p-values and prove greedy recovery under a global reversal-monotone fitness premise. The present score is its exact \(\alpha=1\) population-oracle analogue. The matching-class navigation theorem is therefore not transferred to their full nonlinear class. The included nonlinear separation and trapped-order witnesses are nevertheless members of that broader class and hence transfer only as existential examples; the trap violates the premise needed by Theorem 4.3 and does not refute that conditional theorem. Peters et al. (2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28 on pages 13--16) prove identification under their positive-density restricted-ANM configuration requirement. Their Proposition 17 gives a pointwise nonconstancy characterization of causal minimality, whereas the compact-support model here uses positive-parent-law-measure nonconstancy and a separate relative-interior identification bridge. Reisach et al. (2023, Sections 3 and 5) analyze scale-normalized explained variance, informing the primitive ratios but not the GENE insertion landscape. Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) study covered-arrow walks for a sparsity score rather than GENE insertion ascent. Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) and Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) provide kernel-independence and sample-splitting ingredients but not simultaneous adaptive graph sets with learned normalized risks. Buhlmann, Peters, and Ernest (2014, Theorems 1 and 2) analyze likelihood order estimation and pruning under a different wrong-order variance margin.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The success certificate is sufficient only on matching-component DAGs and is not an observable necessary-and-sufficient boundary for general GENE landscapes. The sharp bivariate trap proves an open failure region inside the identifiable nonlinear-ANM class, but it does not classify the intervening general class. Exact independence remains discontinuous: the population trap handles it by a pointwise support-geometry proof throughout its open structural family, while finite-sample inference requires HSIC separation and otherwise retains both labels. The residual-estimation contribution to the HSIC radius uses the stated nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise. The displayed sample-size order suppresses fixed regularity constants and is sufficient, not minimax optimal.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The delivered population results are a compact-support identification bridge, a matching-subclass insertion-navigation theorem, a six-node strict separation witness, finite-query oracle recovery, a quadratic positive-gain witness, and a sharp open bivariate trapped-order family. The matching-subclass theorem does not establish success on Li et al.'s full nonlinear class; the nonlinear witnesses transfer to that class only existentially, and the trap does not contradict Theorem 4.3 because its global-ranking premise fails there. The simultaneous-band theorem gives direct sufficient conditions \(K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda\), where \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\); absent separation it returns the union of compatible terminal DAGs, which may still be a singleton. No minimax rate or general observable landscape boundary is claimed. The released Sachs workflow remains an audit case: a fixed chi-square threshold does not certify a population margin, and intervention-informed reference directions do not follow from an observational acyclic ANM alone.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem certifies that observational ANM identifiability does not by itself control the exact GENE population landscape: a structurally open family can make the unique wrong-order optimum arbitrarily close to the largest score advantage allowed by \(0\le q\le1\).
statement_notes.gap: The earlier fixed-margin construction did not establish the sharp \(1/2\) boundary or a margin-indexed open family, and treating nonzero HSIC as continuous would have hidden the discontinuity of exact independence.
statement_notes.consumer: Users of population or high-precision GENE optimization obtain an explicit adversarial family and know that the matching-class success certificate cannot be omitted merely because the underlying ANM is identifiable.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and let \(\underline v\) be the constant in Assumption \(\ref{ass:variance-nondegeneracy}\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal X\) supplies a finite bound \(B\) for every coordinate of \(V\) and every clipped residual used below.  All constants denoted by \(K\), \(K_R\), or \(K_H\) may depend on \(B\), the fixed fold proportions, the Holder radius, the two design-density bounds, the kernel bounds, and \(L_k\), but not on \(n\), \(\alpha\), or the particular indices \((v,A,u)\).

We first construct the regression fits and record their simultaneous error.  Fix \(v\in I\), \(A\subseteq I\setminus\{v\}\), and put \(m=|A|\).  Partition \(\mathcal X_A\) into rectangles of side at most \(h\), use polynomials of total degree at most two on each nonempty rectangle, and clip their values to the coordinate range of \(V_v\).  Taylor's formula and Assumption \(\ref{ass:holder-regressions}\) give a member \(g_h\) of this sieve such that
\[
 \lVert g_h-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_\infty\le K h^3. \tag{1}
\]
There are at most \(K h^{-m}\) polynomial coefficients.  For completeness, the usual least-squares bound needed here follows by applying the exponential Markov inequality to the bounded loss differences on each cell and then summing over the cells: the conditional variance of a squared-loss difference is at most \(K\) times its excess squared-error risk, while the sum of the cell dimensions is at most \(K h^{-m}\).  Peeling according to dyadic values of that excess risk and summing the resulting geometric series gives, for the clipped empirical least-squares fit on a training fold of size proportional to \(n\),
\[
 \Pr\left[
 \lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2
 >K\left\{h^6+\frac{h^{-m}+\log(1/\delta)}{n}\right\}
 \right]\le\delta . \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, (1) supplies the comparison element in the empirical least-squares basic inequality; boundedness supplies the displayed variance--mean relation; and on a shell of population excess risk \(r\), the exponential bound is \(\exp\{-c n r+K h^{-m}\}\), which is summable once \(r\ge K\{h^{-m}+\log(1/\delta)\}/n\).  Thus (2) does not require an unrecorded tail or moment hypothesis.

Take \(h=t_n^{1/(m+6)}\) when \(t_n\le1\), and use \(\delta\) proportional to \(\alpha/M_d\).  Since \(m\le d-1\),
\[
 t_n^{3/(m+6)}\le t_n^{3/(d+5)}=a_n.
\]
A union bound over the \(d2^{d-1}\) regressions therefore yields, with probability at least \(1-c\alpha\),
\[
 \max_{v,A}\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}
 \le K a_n. \tag{3}
\]
When \(t_n>1\), clipping and enlargement of \(K\) give (3) directly because both the response and fitted regression are bounded.  Repeating the construction over the fixed number of cross-fitting folds changes only \(K\).

On an evaluation fold independent of a fitted regression, let \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) be the empirical mean of the squared fitted residual.  The defining orthogonality of conditional expectation in Definition \(\ref{def:conditional-risk}\) gives, conditionally on the training fold,
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!left[(V_v-\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A))^2\mid\widehat\mu_{v,A}\right]
 =R_{v,A}+\lVert\widehat\mu_{v,A}-\mu_{v,A}\rVert_{L^2(P_A)}^2. \tag{4}
\]
The evaluation losses are conditionally independent and bounded.  For any centered random variable \(W\) with \(|W|\le b\), convexity of the exponential on \([-b,b]\) gives \(\mathbb E e^{sW}\le e^{s^2b^2/2}\); exponential Markov optimization and a union bound therefore give a simultaneous evaluation error at most \(K\sqrt{t_n}\).  Combining this fact with (3)--(4) produces intervals centered at \(\widehat R_{v,A}\) which contain every \(R_{v,A}\) and whose common half-width obeys
\[
 w_R\le K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n^2\}
 =K_R\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}. \tag{5}
\]

For the HSIC coordinates, use the bounded, centered order-four V-statistic on the evaluation fold, with the off-fold residuals.  Conditional on the training fold, changing one evaluation observation changes this statistic by at most \(K/n\).  The same exponential argument, now exposed one observation at a time, gives deviation \(K\sqrt{t_n}\); terms with repeated indices contribute at most \(K/n\), which is absorbed into that bound.  It remains to compare the population HSIC of fitted and true residuals.  The population HSIC expansion is a fixed sum of expectations of products of bounded kernel factors.  Telescope each product at its residual-kernel factor and apply Assumption \(\ref{ass:residual-kernel-lipschitz}\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and (3) then give
\[
 \left|H_{\widehat\mu}(v,A,u)-H(v,A,u)\right|
 \le K\mathbb E_P\left|\widehat\mu_{v,A}(V_A)-\mu_{v,A}(V_A)\right|
 \le K a_n. \tag{6}
\]
Consequently simultaneous intervals contain all \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\) score-relevant HSIC coordinates and satisfy
\[
 w_H\le K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+a_n\}
 =K_H\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}. \tag{7}
\]
The pruning coordinates have the form \(H(v,A,u)\) with \(u\notin A\).  Their number is at most another \(d(d-1)2^{d-2}\), so the same union bound covers every possibly adaptive pruning query.  This replaces \(M_d\) by at most \(2M_d\); because \(M_d/\alpha\ge2\), \(\log(2M_d/\alpha)\le2\log(M_d/\alpha)\), and the change is absorbed into \(K_H\).  Allocating the preceding failure probabilities so that their sum is at most \(\alpha\) proves the asserted simultaneous coverage probability and the two displayed band rates.

We next make explicit the score-radius consequence that is implicit in interval propagation.  Work on the simultaneous coverage event, suppose all queried HSIC values belong to \(\{0\}\cup[\lambda,\infty)\), and suppose \(2w_H<\lambda\).  If \(H=0\), its interval has upper endpoint at most \(2w_H<\lambda\); if \(H\ge\lambda\), its lower endpoint is at least \(H-2w_H>0\).  Hence Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\) returns the correct singleton label for every queried dependence indicator.

Assume also that \(w_R<\underline v/2\).  Write \(y_v=R_{v,\varnothing}=\operatorname{Var}_P(V_v)\) and \(x_{v,A}=R_{v,A}\).  Conditional expectation is the \(L^2(P)\) projection onto the functions of \(V_A\), so
\[
 0\le x_{v,A}\le y_v,
 \qquad y_v\ge\underline v. \tag{8}
\]
Let \(\widehat y_v\) and \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) be the risk-band centers, and project \(\widehat x_{v,A}\) onto \([0,\widehat y_v]\), denoting the result by \(\widetilde x_{v,A}\).  Coverage and \(w_R<\underline v/2\) imply \(\widehat y_v>0\).  Since \(x_{v,A}\in[0,y_v]\), clipping cannot increase its coordinatewise error, and the possible displacement of the upper clipping endpoint is bounded by \(|\widehat y_v-y_v|\); hence
\[
 |\widetilde x_{v,A}-x_{v,A}|\le w_R,
 \qquad |\widehat y_v-y_v|\le w_R. \tag{9}
\]
Define the feasible propagated center \(\widetilde q(v,A)=1-\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\).  By (8)--(9), \(0\le\widetilde x_{v,A}/\widehat y_v\le1\), and therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\widetilde q(v,A)-q(v,A)|
 &=\left|\frac{x_{v,A}}{y_v}-\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\right|\\
 &\le \frac{|x_{v,A}-\widetilde x_{v,A}|}{y_v}
 +\frac{\widetilde x_{v,A}}{\widehat y_v}\frac{|\widehat y_v-y_v|}{y_v}
 \le \frac{2w_R}{\underline v}. \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
For fixed singleton dependence labels, the multiplier \(1-D(v,A)/(|A|+1)\) in Definition \(\ref{def:gene-score}\) lies in \([0,1]\).  An insertion changes predecessor sets only for the moved node and nodes in the traversed block, at most \(d\) nodes.  Its gain is a difference of the before and after local contributions for precisely those nodes.  Summing (10) over at most \(d\) contributions on each side proves the deterministic propagation bound
\[
 w_S\le K_d w_R,
 \qquad K_d=\frac{4d}{\underline v}=O\!\left(\frac d{\underline v}\right). \tag{11}
\]
The factor four accounts for two local-score sums and the two risk coordinates in each normalized risk.  Thus no continuity of the independence indicator has been used: (11) is asserted only after the separated-label event has made every such indicator fixed.

Combining (5), (7), and (11), choose constants
\[
 K_1\ge \frac{8K_R}{\underline v},
 \qquad K_2\ge2K_H, \tag{12}
\]
enlarging \(K_1\), if necessary, to absorb the fixed regularity constants.  The two direct inequalities
\[
 K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},
 \qquad
 K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda \tag{13}
\]
imply, respectively, \(w_R<\underline v/2\) and \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\), and \(2w_H<\lambda\), after the constants are fixed.  The first implication uses \(d\ge2\) and, for the stated sample-size consequence below, \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\le1\).

At any non-topological order, Theorem \(\ref{thm:pairwise-navigation}\) supplies a correcting insertion with true gain at least \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\).  Coverage and \(2w_S<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) make that insertion positive for every score table compatible with the bands.  Strict score ascent cannot revisit an element of the finite set \(\mathfrak S_I\), so every compatible terminal order is topological.  The now-singleton pruning labels coincide with the population labels used in Theorem \(\ref{thm:oracle-recovery}\); that theorem therefore gives the labelled graph \(G_0\) for every compatible terminal path.  Taking their union proves \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_n=\{G_0\}\).

Finally suppose the regularity constants are fixed and \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}},\lambda\le1\).  Put
\[
 \gamma_d=\max\left\{2,\frac{d+5}{6}\right\},
 \qquad \beta_d=\frac{d+5}{3}.
\]
Since \(\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d\le1\), making \(t_n\) a sufficiently small constant multiple of \((\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}/d)^{\gamma_d}\) controls both terms in the first inequality of (13).  Since \(\beta_d>2\) for \(d\ge2\), making \(t_n\) a sufficiently small constant multiple of \(\lambda^{\beta_d}\) controls both terms in the second.  Hence a direct sufficient sample size is
\[
 n\ge K\log(M_d/\alpha)
 \max\left\{
 \left(\frac d{\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}}\right)^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},
 \lambda^{-(d+5)/3}
 \right\}. \tag{14}
\]
The score-margin exponent equals two through \(d=7\), the two powers coincide at \(d=7\), and the nonparametric power \((d+5)/6\) governs for \(d>7\); this is the score-margin elbow at \(d=7\).  Equation (14) is a sufficient consequence of the proved bands and is not asserted to be minimax optimal.

Without the two separation inequalities, interval propagation never forces a binary label for an HSIC interval meeting both \(0\) and \([\lambda,\infty)\): it retains both labels and returns the union of all compatible terminal DAGs, which may be a singleton or may contain multiple graphs.  This is exactly the set-valued conclusion in Definition \(\ref{def:simultaneous-bands}\), and it completes the proof.
